nationalRESummary.note: RE excluding Large Hydro as per MNRE. Source: mnre.gov.in, as on 30.06.2026

companies.name: Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL)
companies.source: AGEL Press Release Jul 2026 — Surpassed 20 GW operational capacity
companies.notes: India's largest RE company. First to reach 20 GW through greenfield development.

companies.name: ReNew Energy Global Plc
companies.source: ReNew Annual Report FY25; Financial Express Feb 2025
companies.notes: Second largest RE company. Evenly split between solar and wind.

companies.name: Greenko Group
companies.source: Company disclosures; Industry reports
companies.notes: Integrated RE platform with pumped hydro storage. Backed by GIC Singapore & Abu Dhabi's ADIA.

companies.name: Tata Power Renewable Energy
companies.source: Financial Express Feb 2025 — 43% of Tata Power total capacity
companies.notes: RE arm of Tata Power. Strong rooftop solar presence.

companies.name: JSW Energy Ltd (RE Portfolio)
companies.source: JSW Energy Annual Report FY26 — Total capacity 13.2 GW
companies.notes: RE capacity within JSW Energy's total 13.2 GW portfolio. Rapid expansion underway.

companies.name: NTPC Green Energy Ltd
companies.source: NTPC Annual Report FY26; NTPC Green IPO documents
companies.notes: NTPC's renewable energy subsidiary. Targeting 60 GW RE by 2032.

companies.name: Acme Solar Holdings Ltd
companies.source: Acme Solar IPO prospectus; Annual Report FY25
companies.notes: Pure-play solar developer. Projects across Rajasthan, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh.

companies.name: Sembcorp Energy India
companies.source: Sembcorp Industries Annual Report 2025
companies.notes: Singapore-listed Sembcorp's India RE arm. Also has 2.6 GW thermal.

companies.name: Avaada Energy Pvt Ltd
companies.source: ET Energyworld Jun 2026 — 7.2 GWp operational, 17.7 GWp total portfolio
companies.notes: Operational 7.2 GW with 10.5 GW under construction. Targeting 30 GW by 2030. Also has 3 GW solar cell manufacturing.

companies.name: Hero Future Energies
companies.source: Company disclosures; Industry estimates
companies.notes: Hero Group's clean energy arm. Operational across 10+ states.

companies.name: Azure Power Global Ltd
companies.source: Last filed Annual Report; Industry estimates
companies.notes: Pure-play solar. Underwent ownership transition.

companies.name: O2 Power Pvt Ltd
companies.source: Industry reports; EQT portfolio disclosures
companies.notes: Backed by Swedish PE firm EQT and Temasek. Rapid growth platform.

companies.name: SJVN Green Energy Ltd
companies.source: SJVN Annual Report FY26
companies.notes: PSU with strong hydro base expanding into solar and wind.

companies.name: Vibrant Energy
companies.source: Macquarie Asset Management portfolio; Industry estimates
companies.notes: Macquarie-backed RE platform focused on C&I segment.

companies.name: Mytrah Energy (Raksha Energy)
companies.source: Industry estimates; Previously AIM-listed
companies.notes: Rebranded as Raksha Energy. Wind-heavy portfolio.

companies.name: Inox Green Energy Services Ltd
companies.source: Inox Green BSE filings FY26; NSE PR Dec 2025
companies.notes: Wind O&M and IPP arm of Inox Wind. Operates wind farms across GJ, RJ, MP, KA.

companies.name: Serentica Renewables
companies.source: ET Energyworld Sep 2025; serenticaglobal.com — 2,900+ MW operational, 6,750 MW under construction
companies.notes: Operational ~2.9 GW. Targeting 7.5 GW by Dec 2027. Supplies green energy to industrial consumers. 40% portfolio for govt utilities.

companies.name: Amplus Solar (Petronas)
companies.source: Industry reports; Petronas portfolio disclosures
companies.notes: Backed by Malaysian oil major Petronas. Focus on rooftop and open-access solar for C&I.

companies.name: Amp Energy India
companies.source: Company disclosures; Industry estimates 2025-26
companies.notes: Formerly Ampin Energy. Distributed solar and C&I open-access focus.

companies.name: Jakson Green Pvt Ltd
companies.source: Company website; Industry estimates FY25-26
companies.notes: Clean energy arm of Jakson Group. Utility-scale solar EPC and IPP. Expanding into green hydrogen.

companies.name: EDF Renewables India
companies.source: EDF Group Annual Report 2025; Industry estimates
companies.notes: India arm of French utility EDF. Solar and wind projects in southern & western India.

companies.name: Sterlite Power / Vedanta (RE)
companies.source: Vedanta Annual Report FY25; Industry estimates
companies.notes: Primarily captive RE for aluminium smelters. Sterlite Power focuses on transmission infrastructure.

companies.name: Sunsure Energy
companies.source: Company website sunsure-energy.com; PR Newswire Jan 2025 — 700 MW operational, 7.1 GW in development
companies.notes: Round-the-clock RE solutions provider. Target 10 GW by 2030. Recently commissioned 105 MWp in UP.

companies.name: Suzlon Energy Ltd
companies.source: Suzlon BSE filings FY26; CEA Dashboard — operational IPP capacity
companies.notes: India's largest wind turbine manufacturer. Also operates own wind farms. Order book 5.1 GW. Market leader in domestic wind OEM.

companies.name: Sprng Energy (Shell)
companies.source: Shell New Energies disclosures; NPP registered capacity data 2025-26
companies.notes: Acquired by Shell in 2022 for $1.55 bn. Solar & wind projects across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh.

companies.name: Continuum Green Energy
companies.source: GRID-INDIA registered generator data; Industry reports 2025
companies.notes: Backed by Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners. Balanced solar-wind portfolio. Operational in 6 states.

companies.name: Waaree Energies (IPP arm)
companies.source: Waaree Energies Annual Report FY26; BSE filings
companies.notes: India's largest solar module manufacturer (12 GW capacity). Also developing own solar farms for IPP revenue.

companies.name: NHPC Ltd (RE Division)
companies.source: NHPC Annual Report FY26; CEA capacity additions register
companies.notes: Traditionally hydro-focused PSU expanding into solar. Commissioned solar projects in Rajasthan, UP, and Madhya Pradesh.

companies.name: NLC India Ltd (RE)
companies.source: NLC India Annual Report FY26; CEA Dashboard registered capacity
companies.notes: Lignite major diversifying into RE. Solar parks in Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan. 10 GW RE target by 2030.

companies.name: Torrent Power Ltd (RE)
companies.source: Torrent Power Annual Report FY26; IEX market participant data
companies.notes: Gujarat-based utility with gas + solar + wind portfolio. Active on IEX power exchange. Expanding RE for distribution.

companies.name: CleanMax Enviro Energy
companies.source: Company disclosures; NPP open access generation data FY25-26
companies.notes: Leading C&I solar provider. 850+ corporate clients. Hybrid solar-wind-storage solutions for industries.

companies.name: Fourth Partner Energy
companies.source: TPG Rise Fund disclosures; Company website fourthpartner.co
companies.notes: TPG-backed distributed solar company. Rooftop and open-access for 350+ commercial clients across India.

companies.name: Axis Energy Ventures (KKR)
companies.source: KKR portfolio disclosures; GRID-INDIA generator registration records
companies.notes: KKR's India RE platform. Acquired Ramky group's solar assets. Building 5 GW portfolio.

companies.name: Coal India Ltd (Solar arm)
companies.source: Coal India Annual Report FY26; CIL Solar division disclosures
companies.notes: Irony: World's largest coal miner is setting up solar on mine-lands. Target 3 GW solar by 2028. Using degraded mine land.

companies.name: Vikram Solar (IPP)
companies.source: Company disclosures; CEA capacity register FY26
companies.notes: Top solar module manufacturer (3.5 GW production). Small IPP arm with own solar farms in West Bengal, Rajasthan.
